facts.statement: Nanocetorhinus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fish belonging to the subclass Neoselachii.
facts.quote: Nanocetorhinus is an extinct genus of cartilaginous fishes in the subclass Neoselachii from the Late Oligocene to Middle Miocene.

facts.statement: The species N. tuberculatus was described in 2013 by Underwood and Schlogl based on 28 fossilized teeth found in Slovakia.
facts.quote: Nanocetorhinus tuberculatus was described by Underwood and Schlogl in 2013, from 28 partial and complete fossilized teeth (holotype: Z 27485) discovered in the Laksarska Nova Ves Formation at Cerová-Lieskové, Vienna Basin, in Slovakia.

facts.statement: A second species, N. zeitlingeri, was named in 2020 based on three complete fossilized teeth found in Austria.
facts.quote: In 2020, Feichtinger, Pollerspöck and Harzhauser named a second species N. zeitlingeri based on three complete fossilized teeth from the Kamig quarry in Austria.

facts.statement: The genus name combines "nano" meaning dwarfish and "Cetorhinus" the basking shark, referencing the small resemblance of its teeth to those of the basking shark.
facts.quote: The generic name combines the Latin term "nano" ("dwarvish") with "Cetorhinus" (the generic name of the basking shark), and references the resemblance the teeth of Nanocetorhinus bear to those of Cetorhinus, but on a smaller scale.

facts.statement: Researchers theorized that Nanocetorhinus was a planktivorous shark, though this is not supported by evidence of close relation to the basking shark.
facts.quote: Underwood and Schlogl theorized that Nanocetorhinus was a planktivorous shark, similarly to its namesake, although there is no consequential evidence that the two genera are closely related.

facts.statement: The largest teeth of Nanocetorhinus were no more than 1 millimeter long.
facts.quote: The teeth were little more than 1 mm long at the largest.

facts.statement: The teeth were simple and irregular with no wear on the cutting edges, suggesting they played a minimal role in grabbing or puncturing meat.
facts.quote: The authors described the form of the teeth as "simple and rather irregular", and mentioned a lack of wear on the cutting edges, indicating that they were not used to grab and puncture meat, but rather played a minimal role in the process of food consumption.

facts.statement: Nanocetorhinus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Nanocetorhinus lived between 23.04 and 13.82 million years ago, from the Aquitanian to the Langhian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Aquitanian to Langhian (23.04 to 13.82 million years ago)

rejected.statement: The type species N. tuberculatus lived across the Northern Hemisphere during the Early to Middle Miocene, while the second species N. zeitlingeri lived in Austria during the Late Oligocene.
rejected.quote: The type species N. tuberculatus lived across the Northern Hemisphere during the Early to Middle Miocene, and the second species N. zeitlingeri lived in Austria during the Late Oligocene.
